result.topic_en: Euler argues that a column's resistance to breaking can be modelled by an elastic lamina that bends under its own weight into the curve derived earlier, and he begins to examine portions of that curve as equilibrium states, particularly points with vertical tangents taken as fixed lower ends.

items.english: For one can always conceive an elastic lamina which resists bending as much as the column resists breaking.

items.quote:
Abſciſſae autem huius curuae ad eo maiorem altitudinem
aſſurgent, quo fortiores fuerint laminae noſtrae elaſticae:
applicatae vero, ſingulis abſciſſis reſpondentes, perpetuo ean-
dem inter ſe rationem tenere ſunt cenſendae.
items.english: The abscissas of this curve rise to a greater height the stronger our elastic laminae are, while the ordinates corresponding to the individual abscissas must be considered always to keep the same ratio among themselves.

items.english: Any portion of this curve, such as AY, will represent the equilibrium state of some elastic lamina.

items.english: If any of these points is taken as the lowest end of the elastic lamina, it must also be fixed vertically into the floor, so that it cannot deviate from this position.
